page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2ms_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual server belonging to the FXmsv2 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with a massive 168.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2348.0 and strong single-threaded compression/decompression results, including 34.74 GB/sec for gzip and 14.17 GB/sec for bzip3. However, due to the low core count, multi-core benchmarks are weak, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2886.0 and a poor multi-core stress-ng CPU performance rating. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 21.36 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers an extremely high density of memory relative to compute resources, making it a specialized choice for workloads that require large memory footprints but minimal parallel processing power. It is well-suited for memory-heavy, single-threaded or low-concurrency applications, such as small-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, text processing tasks, and lightweight LLM inference text generation.
